title: cloud: at the framework bump carrying #26485, check the hosted kernel records missed scheduled runs (persisted dispatch ledger, sys_job arming) and unblock cloud#3149 item 5
body:
Filed by the `domain:server` seat 1 under the maintainer's word for cloud items surfaced during development, verbatim: 「需要转给 cloud的，应该立 cloud 车道卡」 and 「开发中涉及 cloud 车道的，也应该转给 cloud」. Parked here with `domain:cloud` + `status:parked` + `repo:cloud` until the cloud PM moves it, as pm-dispatch's `domain:cloud` row says. ⛔ Not a claim; this repository does not dispatch it.

**Origin:** objectstack-ai/objectstack#25235, filed from objectstack-ai/cloud#3149 item 5 (cloud#3149 is `Blocked-by:` it). Fixed by PR #26485, merged as `2282aa8ed5`; the card closed as completed. When a hosted kernel is stopped, evicted or restarting, the next kernel to bind each scheduled flow now records every due time that passed in the silence as one run-history entry with status `missed`: `startedAt` is the due time and `completedAt` the detection. Nothing is replayed. The entries are listed by `listRuns` and `GET /api/v1/automation/:name/runs?status=missed`. Patch changesets: `@objectstack/trigger-schedule`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-job`.

**What cloud should do with it:**
- cloud#3149 item 5 loses its `Blocked-by:` once cloud's framework pin carries `2282aa8ed5`.
- Detection needs a persisted dispatch ledger (`sys_flow_dispatch`). An engine running with the in-process-only dedup (its one-time warning 「trigger dispatch dedup is IN-PROCESS ONLY」) skips detection with one warn per flow and records nothing. Check that the hosted kernel runs with the persisted ledger, or cloud gets no `missed` rows at all.
- Detection also reads `sys_job` arming through `DbJobAdapter.readArming`. A hosted kernel on another job adapter records nothing.
- `FlowTrigger` gains an optional `release(flowName)`, which the engine calls when its scheduled-work policy refuses a flow. A cloud-side trigger implementation compiles unchanged, but without `release` a policy-OFF kernel leaves an armed row behind that a later kernel can read as a silence.
- `packages/service-ai-studio/src/verify/clock-trigger-arming.ts` (cloud) records that the gap exists. Once the bump lands, it can assert one `missed` row per due time instead.

**Done when:** at the cloud PR that moves the framework pin past `2282aa8ed5`, an evicted-then-reopened hosted environment shows one `missed` run per passed due time for a scheduled flow (read through `?status=missed`), and cloud#3149 item 5 is closed against it.

Blocked-by: the framework release that carries PR #26485.
